questions.question: Select the odd group of numbers. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13–Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.solution:
The pattern followed is:

First \: number over10 = Second number 

Second \: number over10 = Third number

Let us check each option:

1. (400 – 40 – 4) 

The pattern followed here is:

⇒400over10 = 40 

⇒ 40over 10 = 4 

Then, it will be (400 – 40 – 4).

2. (300 – 30 – 7) 

The pattern followed here is: 

⇒300over10 = 30 

⇒30 - 23 = 7 

Then, it will be (300 – 30 – 7). 

3. (1000 – 100 – 10) 

The pattern followed here is:

⇒ 1000over10 = 100 

⇒100over10 = 10 

Then, it will be (1000 – 100 – 10) 

4. (500 – 50 – 5) 

The pattern followed here is: 

⇒500over 10 = 50 

⇒50 over 10 = 5 

Then, it will be (500 – 50 – 5).

**The pattern followed is:**

First \: number over10 = Second number 

Second \: number over10 = Third number

Option 1, Option 3 and Option 4 have the same pattern only Option 2 has a different one then, and the odd one out is Option 2.

Hence, the correct answer is **'Option 2'.**

questions.question: If A – B means that A is the brother of B, A + B means that A is the sister of B, A ÷ B means that A is the father of B then which of the following expression shows that P is the paternal uncle of R?
questions.solution:
Family Chart:

 [IMAGE: https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/FyD9L3PCPvZsHa5nynlMPf_fzf_aXK9tKopSaDWxBYVwFRo-6fzjiv7HQG28YUhFJ0nLGj9_hEV_JqW5NQsWS_FX2dnhd3UTkTZ5DE4dKFyqgfFDku2-8QBz2pL7YIeD6iwR5lii] 

Given:

'A – B' means that 'A is the brother of B'.

'A + B' means that 'A is the sister of B'.

'A ÷ B' means that 'A is the father of B'.

Let us first decode the given symbols and Family chart:

 
 

 Symbols
 Meanings
 
 

 A – B
 A is the brother of B
 
 

 A + B
 A is the sister of B
 
 

 A ÷ B
 A is the father of B
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4eb751f2d6fa3bf5fdc79cdf0a1faf42b82c998f1ad22b942b9cd7cd62d2f4a1.png] 

Now, let us check all the options.

1) P + Q ÷ R → False (P is the sister of Q and Q is the father of R).

2) P ÷ Q – R → False (P is the father of Q and Q is the brother of R).

3) P – Q ÷ R →** True **(P is the brother of Q and Q is the father of R that means P is the paternal uncle of R).

4) P – Q + R → False (P is the brother of Q and Q is the sister of R).

Hence, '**P – Q ÷ R'**** is** the correct answer.

questions.question:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All gorillas are bears.

All pigs are bears.

All bears are tigers.

**Conclusions:**

I. All pigs are tigers.

II. All tigers are gorillas.

III. Some tigers are pigs.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow

questions.solution:
Statements:
All gorillas are bears.
All pigs are bears.
All bears are tigers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/87ed1620af142e0a7ab6468663c7c620cd88e057ca7ca014ff3a3a4ff029303f.png] 
Conclusions:
I. All pigs are tigers → Follow → Since 'All pigs are bears.' and 'All bears are tigers.' we can say that All pigs are tigers and the same can be seen in the Venn diagram so the conclusion follows.
II. All tigers are gorillas → Does not follow → From the given statements 'All gorillas are bears.' and 'All bears are tigers.' Therefore 'All tigers are gorillas' is a possibility and the same can be seen in the Venn diagram so the conclusion does not follows.
III. Some tigers are pigs → Follow → Since 'All pigs are bears.' and 'All bears are tigers.' we can say that Some pigs are tigers and the same can be seen in the Venn diagram so the conclusion follows.

Hence, **Only conclusions I and III follow.**
